14-quality-and-procurement.html 8/10. A newcomer would be least sure about who carries the risk in each contract type: the text and the table disagree on time-and-materials, and seller and buyer are never defined.

15-communication-and-handover.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on agile words such as "sprints" and "go-live" in one example, and on a loosely worded ranking of communication channels; the rest is plain and the quizzes teach their answers.

24-mixed-scenario-drill.html 8/10, 29-motivation-and-team-stages.html 7/10. A newcomer would stall on the motivation step: three ideas are promised but never named, pay appears both as a basic need and as a hygiene factor, and 'sponsor' and 'PMP' are used without a plain explanation. The stages step is clear.
29-motivation-and-team-stages.html 8/10.

38-technical-practices.html 8/10. A newcomer who knows Python would follow most of this, but would not know what an automated test is or why it must fail first, and would trip on "library" and "load" in the spike example.
